name: Single-arm cable pulldown
cue: Half-kneeling, drive the elbow down to your hip.
research: Half-kneeling single-arm cable pulldown, right arm working, facing a high pulley (1.22 H, 2.2 m, on a column 0.36 H, 0.64 m, in front of the lifter and 0.13 H to the right of the midline): the right knee on a knee mat with the shin flat behind (hip 0, knee 90, foot plantar flexed 40), the left foot flat on a plate in front (hip 90, knee 90, the shank vertical), the left hand resting on the left knee, the trunk upright and still. Design values from the standard technique description, not a measured trial: the right arm starts reaching up and forward to the handle (shoulder elevation 150, plane 85, elbow 15, the hand 0.94 H high and 0.14 H ahead of the trunk, the shoulder blade rotated up: clavicle elevation 16, protraction 6) and the elbow is pulled down in front of the body and then to the side (elevation 15, plane 20, elbow flexion 100: the elbow beside the ribs, 0.41 H high at the trunk line, the hand ending 0.49 H high in front of the lower chest, the shoulder blade depressed and drawn back: clavicle elevation -4, protraction -12). The stirrup handle rides on the fist (a free-swinging triangle on the grip bar that follows the cable, dswing; the bar is kept square to the cable). The cable runs from the pulley down and back, clear of the head and trunk in every phase (closest 0.11 H to the arm, 0.16 H to the trunk). Cable 1:1 to the stack, 0.40 H of travel. Geometry: design/cableA/pd.mjs.

targets.note: design values (standard technique), not a measured trial; the plane read-back is thorax-relative

camera.note: View from behind and a little to the right, slightly raised (az 165, el 12, 17 deg off the view from behind): the working-side lat opens out under the shoulder blade as the elbow drives down and spreads as it sweeps to the side; the column stands beyond the figure and the cable runs away from the camera up to the pulley.

skinChecks.note: the front sole stays on its plate
the back shin rests on the knee mat
